signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the same average over an interval of length one; a correct answer there with a wrong answer elsewhere points at the missing division rather than at the integral.
signals.name: Correct integral with no division by the interval length
signals.observation: The response shows the correct definite integral and reports its value, with no quotient anywhere.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of the reported answer; rate units confirm the confusion with average rate of change.
signals.name: Difference quotient produced where an average value was requested
signals.observation: The response computes the change in the function divided by the change in the input and calls it the average value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the displacement in the same part; a correct displacement with an equal answer for distance isolates the integrand choice.
signals.name: Signed integral reported as total distance
signals.observation: The response integrates velocity across a sign change and reports the result as the distance travelled.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the same question with a different starting amount; an unchanged answer confirms that the initial value is not in the model.
signals.name: Accumulated change reported where an amount was asked
signals.observation: The definite integral is evaluated correctly and reported without the known value at the earlier time.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the value of the amount at each endpoint; producing them on request separates a reporting gap from a conceptual one.
signals.name: Critical point found with only a local justification
signals.observation: The derivative is set equal to zero and solved correctly, and the justification is a sign chart with no endpoint comparison and no uniqueness statement.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the sentence would be for a different pair of limits; a correct second sentence points at a communication habit rather than a concept gap.
signals.name: Interpretation naming the quantity and units but not the interval
signals.observation: The sentence gives the accumulated quantity with correct units and omits the two inputs bounding the accumulation.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which curve is above the other at one interior input; a correct answer there isolates the sign slip.
signals.name: Negative value reported as an area or a volume
signals.observation: The integral is set up with the difference in the wrong order and the reported value is negative.

signals.distinguish_by: Recompute with the stored values; agreement confirms a rounding habit rather than a set up error.
signals.name: Stored intersection values replaced by rounded decimals
signals.observation: The limits appear as two or three place decimals and the reported area differs from the correct value in the third decimal place.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to name the variable of integration and to list the variables in the integrand.
signals.name: Differential dy attached to an integrand written in x
signals.observation: The integral carries dy with an integrand that still contains x, and the limits may be x values.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the sign of the integrand just above and just below the crossing.
signals.name: One integral spanning an interior crossing
signals.observation: The response writes one integral of a fixed difference over an interval in which the curves exchange places.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which shape the area formula inside the integral belongs to.
signals.name: Factor of pi in a polygonal cross section integrand
signals.observation: The volume integral for square or triangular sections carries pi.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of a semicircle of stated radius; a correct answer isolates the radius error from the halving error.
signals.name: Full circle area used for a semicircular section
signals.observation: The integrand is pi times the square of half the distance with no factor of one half, or pi times the square of the whole distance.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the area of one circular slice before the integral is assembled.
signals.name: Solid of revolution volume reported without pi
signals.observation: The integrand is the square of the radius with no constant factor.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to compute both expressions with the radii five and three.
signals.name: Washer integrand written as one squared difference
signals.observation: The integrand is pi times the square of the difference of the two functions.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the distance from a named point on the curve to the axis of revolution.
signals.name: Radius written as the bare function value about a shifted axis
signals.observation: The axis of revolution is a line other than a coordinate axis and the radius in the integrand contains no reference to it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which curve is farther from the axis at one interior input.
signals.name: Negative volume from exchanged radii
signals.observation: The washer integral evaluates to a negative number and the response reports it or its absolute value without comment.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the limits of integration describe; naming them on request separates a reporting gap from a concept gap.
signals.name: Arc length named with no interval
signals.observation: The response says the integral gives the length of the curve and stops.
